concepts.definition: the condition in which limited resources are insufficient to satisfy all human wants
the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made
the quantity of a good or service consumers are willing and able to buy at various prices over a period
the quantity of a good or service producers are willing and able to offer at various prices over a period
the market condition in which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied at a particular price
a sustained rise in the general price level that reduces the purchasing power of money
the condition of people able and willing to work who cannot obtain employment
the monetary value of final goods and services produced within a country's borders during a specified period
a measure of how responsive one economic variable is to a change in another variable
an arrangement through which buyers and sellers interact to exchange goods, services, or resources
